Widen the orchestration test bounds that host load can exceed (#284)

On a loaded host, 3 checks in the orchestration suites failed although
the code under test ended normally. The hook starts the enumerator's
timeout clock when it starts the child (subprocess.run at
aiqt_hooks.py:22833), so the 5 second enumerator timeout of the test
registries also covered interpreter start-up; the stamp test bounded
the enumerator's whole-second stamp to 5 seconds from a clock read
taken before the enumerator started; and the enumerator timeout case
of the stage-2 suite bounded the whole hook run, start-up included, to
15 seconds. This closes TODO 254.

tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py adds the module constant ENUM_TIMEOUT,
60 seconds, with a comment that gives its reason, and uses it in place
of 5 at the 3 fixture registries whose enumerator should end normally:
stage2(), _arm_writing_enumerator and the doctor disclosure case. 60
is the hook's own fallback (aiqt_hooks.py:22831) and stays below the
120 second bound of run_hook, so the hook still reports an enumerator
that hangs. The 2 registries whose argv is malformed by design keep 5,
since no child starts there. In the enumerator timeout case the bound
on the hook run goes from 15 to 45 seconds and the sleep of its
enumerator from 30 to 60 seconds, so a hook that waited the sleep out
still fails the case.

tools/test-orch-enumerate-backlog.py runs the real enumerator through
ENUMERATE_PROG under a 60 second timeout instead of 5. The stamp test,
renamed test_generated_at_utc_is_stamped_while_the_enumerator_runs,
requires that the stamp lie between the clock before the run,
truncated to the second, and the clock after it. The enumerator
truncates its stamp to whole seconds, so the lower bound is exact, and
the test now refuses a stale stamp that the old window accepted.

tools/test-orchestration-registry.py is unchanged: its timeouts of 5
are data that the registry gate checks, no child runs under them, and
the gate refuses any timeout outside (0, 8]. The test registries of
the 2 changed suites never reach the gate.

Checks that fail without the change, each a fixed start-up delay in a
scratch copy: a 6 s fixture enumerator start fails 4 stage-2 cases; a
6 s real enumerator start fails the hook case and the stamp test of
the enumerate-backlog suite; a 16 s hook start fails the enumerator
timeout case at 17.57 s. Each passes with the change. Controls: a 46 s
hook start still fails the 45 s bound, a 70 s enumerator is still cut
at 60 s, and an enumerator stamp 3 s stale passes the old stamp test
but fails the new one. Under load from busy processes pinned with the
test to 1 CPU, the unchanged tree failed the enumerator timeout case at
32-fold and 64-fold, test_stage2_allows at 128-fold and the hook case
of the enumerate-backlog suite at 96-fold. With the change those cases
passed at 64-fold, 128-fold and 96-fold; the 32-fold run was not
repeated with the change. With the change and no added load,
the stage-2 suite ran 142 tests OK, the enumerate-backlog suite 95 and
the registry suite 177. The label suite failed the same 2 cases on the
unchanged tree as with the change, both from git ls-files in a copy
that is not a git repository.

Residuals: a wider bound makes a load failure rarer, not impossible;
at 128-fold the unchanged tree's enumerator timeout case took 71.15 s,
over the new 45 s bound, and 1 stage-2 case exceeded the 120 s bound of
run_hook, which this change leaves as it is. An enumerator that hangs
now holds a test run for up to 60 s. The fixture value 60 is safe only
while the test registries are never gated. The new stamp test fails on
a backward clock step during the run. Each load run is 1 sample on a
shared host. DoctorScopeMargin, the 8 second PreToolUse budget, the
bounds of 20 seconds and more, load other than CPU contention and a
run of the label suite in a git checkout are not covered.
